Yes—for Codex, the current code indicates that `mj-memory` tools disappear when the harness is relaunched to resume a session. That’s a bug.

We already fixed this exact failure for `mj-agents` in commit [`e6bf0f7f`](https://github.com/BrokkAi/mjolnir/commit/e6bf0f7f): Codex rebuilds its MCP configuration from the load/resume request. That fix explicitly left project memory excluded in [launch.rs](/workspace/249b620ea02209220090ad4aec3ba746/hel/mj-worker/src/acp/launch.rs:203).

The distinction matters:

- The saved memory documents remain intact; access through the MCP tools is lost.
- Reattaching the UI to an already-running harness doesn’t trigger this.
- Claude’s native memory is unaffected; harnesses configured through profile files follow a different path.

The exclusion cites a history-replay problem. We should fix that problem while preserving tools across resume, rather than accept losing memory access. My previous wording made this sound like a valid lifecycle constraint; it’s an existing defect to address before extending `mj-memory`.

Yes—there’s a separate `provenance` skill for `trace`, `blame`, and listing files changed by a session. I’ll include both skills in the move to `mj-memory`, along with the resume fix, and check the interfaces and harness setup needed for an implementation-ready plan.

The resume fix can be a separate first milestone. Provenance has an extra complication: line attribution needs Git data from the session’s actual checkout, while the session index stays on the controller. I’m checking the library API so the plan handles container and SSH paths correctly.

Two findings affect the plan. The pinned Claude adapter does accept MCP servers in launch requests, so `mj-memory` can use that route on macOS without editing the user’s profile. The repository comments saying otherwise are stale.

Also, Mjolnir currently indexes its own sessions with an empty changed-file list. Moving provenance into MCP will need to populate that data; otherwise the tools would miss Mjolnir sessions.

> Mjolnir currently indexes its own sessions with an empty changed-file list

tbc this is a bug no matter where provenance tool lives right?

Yes. It’s an existing indexing bug, independent of whether provenance is exposed through a CLI, MCP, or anything else.

Mjolnir’s adapter explicitly returns `touched: Vec::new()` and `edits: Vec::new()`, even though its stored tool calls contain file paths and edit evidence. That makes its sessions invisible to file-based provenance queries. Native sessions indexed by other adapters may still appear, masking the gap.

I’ll make fixing that—and backfilling sessions whose source records or checkpoints remain available—a separate milestone in the plan. Already-pruned sessions may lack enough retained evidence to reconstruct their changed-file lists.

# Preserve memory tools on resume and move recall/provenance into `mj-memory`

## Summary

Deliver three independently validated changes: fix tools disappearing on resume, repair Mjolnir’s missing provenance data, and expose recall and provenance through the existing `mj-memory` MCP server.

The separate managed `recall` and `provenance` skills will be retired. Their guidance will move into MCP instructions and tool descriptions. SessionWiki remains a Rust library on the controller; targets need neither its binary nor its database.

Use an ExecPlan at `.agents/plans/memory-recall-provenance.md` during implementation, following `.agents/PLANS.md`.

## 1. Fix tool delivery across session lifecycles

- Assemble Mjolnir-owned MCP definitions through one launch helper and include the applicable servers in new, load, and resume requests. Recompute target-specific commands and paths after checkpoint restoration or a move.
- Remove the rule in `mj-worker/src/acp/launch.rs` that excludes project memory on resume. Preserve replay suppression and rejection of delayed updates for historical tool calls; tool availability must not depend on suppressing server registration.
- Keep existing harness-specific delivery where necessary, including Kimi’s staged profile. Ensure each server is registered once.
- Test both load-with-replay and resume-without-replay, including bridge crashes and worker restarts. Existing native-child replay must continue working.
- Commit this fix independently, before adding history tools.

Acceptance: a Codex session can write a memory document, close/resume or recover from a bridge restart, then read and update that document through MCP without duplicating its old transcript.

## 2. Repair provenance indexing independently

Mjolnir’s SessionWiki adapter currently returns empty `touched` and `edits` lists. Fix the source of that missing data.

- Add one shared extractor for successful ACP file-edit evidence. Use structured diff paths and edit locations from both live projections and checkpoint transcripts. Exclude reads, failed edits, and paths mentioned only in prose.
- Populate touched files and bounded edit evidence where retained content supports it. Reuse stored diff helpers; compacted records that retain only paths still contribute file provenance.
- Preserve recorded paths. Normalize separators only at the index boundary; do not resolve a historical target path against the controller’s filesystem.
- Backfill recoverable existing sessions in the controller’s background indexer. Track a per-session extraction revision using existing index metadata, and commit provenance updates and that revision together. Retry failures without marking them complete.
- Keep session IDs, annotations, summaries, and archived transcripts intact. Do not rebuild the entire index or change its schema merely to refresh extraction.
- Explicitly report incomplete historical coverage where original records and checkpoints have already been pruned.

Acceptance: edits made in a Mjolnir session become discoverable by file, including after checkpointing and archiving. Previously indexed sessions are repaired when their evidence remains available.

## 3. Extend `mj-memory` with recall and provenance

Select capabilities at server startup:

| Harness | Advertised capabilities |
|---|---|
| Claude | Recall and provenance; native project memory remains unchanged |
| Codex, Grok, Kimi | Existing document `list`/`read`/`write`, plus recall and provenance |
| Muse | No new MCP support; its adapter currently lacks injection support |

Use ACP registration for Claude’s new `mj-memory` server. Inspection of pinned `claude-agent-acp` 0.79.0 confirms it consumes `mcpServers` on new/load/resume requests. This also avoids modifying the user’s profile on local macOS. Correct stale comments about Claude’s support without expanding this work into unrelated MCP migrations.

Add these tools:

| Tool | Contract |
|---|---|
| `search_sessions` | Search the controller’s existing corpus; return session IDs, titles, projects, snippets, and index freshness. |
| `get_session_brief` | Return a bounded briefing for one session. |
| `search_session` | Find literal text within a session, with bounded neighboring messages and message indices. |
| `read_session` | Read a page starting at a message index; optional role filtering supports user-turn outlines. |
| `trace_file` | Return sessions that recorded edits to a path, with the matched recorded paths. |
| `session_files` | Return a paginated list of files a session changed. |
| `blame_file` | Attribute a requested line range using Git evidence from the target and session evidence from the controller. |

Use explicit session IDs from results. Reject ambiguous prefixes. Message indices remain those of the indexed transcript, including when filtering roles.

Default discovery pages to 20 results, capped at 100. Default transcript pages to 20 messages with a 16,000-character text budget, capped at 64,000. Return continuation information and explicit truncation indicators. Mark missing timestamps and unavailable original transcript content honestly.

All new tools are read-only. Search covers the same corpus as the existing session viewer. Continuing or restoring a session remains outside this toolset.

## 4. Transport, concurrency, and migration

- Add a typed history-query channel between the worker and controller, following the existing delegation request/response pattern but independent of delegation enablement. A session with subagents disabled must still have history tools.
- Use bounded, transient pending requests with request IDs, a 60-second deadline, and cleanup on disconnection or expiry. Controller work runs in supervised background tasks. Failed or timed-out requests return explicit tool errors.
- Keep history data on the controller and document operations on the target’s existing memory replica. No database mounts, replicated history index, web-viewer dependency, or full daemon API token on targets.
- Run MCP requests concurrently while serializing document-store operations to preserve compare-and-swap behavior. Slow history queries must not block local memory access; shutdown must cancel waiting work and remain bounded.
- For `blame_file`, resolve the path relative to the session’s working directory and run Git on that target through shared subprocess helpers. Send bounded blame evidence to the controller for SessionWiki attribution. Preserve confident/ambiguous/unattributed outcomes and label attribution as heuristic. Uncommitted lines remain unattributed; Git failures are errors, not silent substitutes for line attribution.
- Match provenance using recorded paths and repository-relative tails, returning the actual matches. Do not silently broaden a failed path query to its basename or imply that equal suffixes prove repository identity.
- Bump and negotiate the relay protocol for the new messages. Preserve legacy document-only operation for older launch configurations; enable history capabilities through the normal worker upgrade/relaunch path.
- Remove the two packaged skills from managed installation after the MCP replacement is complete. Normal reconciliation removes obsolete managed copies from session-owned homes; preserve user-owned skills. Carry over guidance to search selectively, cite session IDs, and treat retrieved conversations as historical evidence.
- Keep existing index-version mismatch protection and background freshness handling. No Mjolnir database migration is expected.

## 5. Validation and delivery

- Exercise actual MCP calls before and after new/load/resume, bridge restart, checkpoint restore, and target relocation. Verify Claude receives history tools without duplicate document tools or changes to its user profile.
- Test replayed historical tool events, delayed updates, and native-child replay alongside successful post-resume tool calls.
- Test the complete recall sequence: search → matching message → surrounding transcript. Include archived sessions, Unicode, missing/ambiguous IDs, pagination, and oversized messages.
- Test provenance for live, checkpointed, compacted, and backfilled sessions; reads and failed edits must not count. Include identical filenames in different repositories, paths containing spaces or SQL wildcard characters, deleted files, and uncertain blame results.
- Test container/SSH path differences, disabled delegation, controller disconnection/reconnection, request expiry, concurrent document writes, and responsive shutdown. Use payloads exceeding 64 KB for pipe/transport tests.
- Run live acceptance with Codex and Claude, including resume, plus container and SSH targets. Use isolated configuration, data, and SessionWiki stores.
- Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test`, and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` in the dev profile. Commit each validated milestone to the current branch; do not push or close #1066 as part of this implementation.

The acceptance boundary is usable tools and repaired indexing—not merely advertised tool definitions. Historical data that was already discarded cannot be reconstructed and must remain an explicit coverage limitation.
